notes.trap: The second argument is a Java regex, not a literal delimiter. A bare '.' matches every character. Trailing empty strings are kept, unlike Java's default split.
The delimiter is a literal string, not a regex. An out-of-range partNum returns an empty string rather than NULL, and partNum 0 raises an error.
Positions are 1-based, but pos 0 is silently treated like pos 1. Other engines such as PostgreSQL count position 0 as one character before the start, so they return one character fewer.
A negative pos counts from the end of the string, and len is then applied going forward from that point.
A negative count returns everything to the right of the count-th delimiter, counted from the right. The delimiter match is case-sensitive.

In trim(trimStr FROM str), trimStr is a set of characters, not a substring. Any combination of those characters is stripped from both ends. Note the argument order: the characters to remove come before FROM.
The one-argument form removes only the space character (0x20). Trailing tabs and newlines are kept.
If the first character is not a letter, the input string is returned unchanged rather than a Soundex code or NULL.
A negative n returns an empty string instead of NULL or an error.
When fmt is omitted the default is 'hex', not 'utf-8', so a string like 'abc' is parsed as hex digits. An odd-length hex string is left-padded with a 0 nibble.
A format digit '9' pads unused positions with spaces, not zeros. Use '0' to get zero padding.
`to_varchar(...)` is only an alias of `to_char(...)` for numbers. It is not a cast to VARCHAR. A format starting with '0' zero-pads the integer part.
The result is a DECIMAL whose precision and scale come from the format string, not from the input value. Inputs that do not match the format raise an error.
A '9' sequence can match the same number of digits or fewer, but never more. An input with too many digits for the format gives NULL here, whereas `to_number(...)` would raise an error.
When `from` is longer than `to`, the extra characters in `from` are deleted from the input rather than left unchanged.
